items.review_rationale: Read associative Boolean ring with required unity and idempotence of all elements, distinguishing the unital convention from the separate nonunital variant.

references.context: Ring with additive abelian group and associative distributive multiplication, possessing a specified two-sided identity.
Universal multiplicative idempotence throughout R, not just for selected idempotents.

references.phrase: unital convention versus nonunital Boolean ring
references.disposition: Unity is an explicit additional structural assumption and is not silently imposed on the other variant.

items.review_rationale: Read Borel sigma-algebra generated by every open subset of a topological space as the least sigma-algebra, including equivalent intersection over all containing sigma-algebras.

references.phrase: subset tau of the power set of X
generated sigma-algebra from open family tau
references.context: Smallest sigma-algebra on X that contains all sets open in topology tau.

references.phrase: intersection of all containing sigma algebras
references.context: Intersection of the family of sigma algebras on X with tau included; this satisfies the same sigma-algebra axioms.

references.disposition: The topology tau is essential input; Borel sigma-algebra is not generally the full power set.

items.review_rationale: Read real antiderivative as differentiable function F on an open interval whose pointwise derivative equals the given f everywhere, and retained the shared interval.

references.phrase: derivative function on an open interval

references.context: Interval in R that is open in usual topology; each x is an interior point suitable for derivative.
For every x in I, the finite derivative of F exists and agrees with f's value.

references.disposition: If one exists, adding real constants gives others; equality of the derivative alone does not select a unique F.

items.review_rationale: Read indefinite integral as family of all constant shifts of an antiderivative on the same interval, distinct from a Riemann or Lebesgue definite integral.

references.phrase: antiderivative F of f on I

references.context: Set of functions x↦F(x)+C for all real constants C, each on the same interval I.
Constant real-valued function on I, whose derivative is zero.

references.phrase: symbol indefinite integral does not denote a single number
references.disposition: It denotes a family of functions, not a definite integral over an interval.
